title: Campus Customs MCP smoke test
problem: Problem 4 — Add the MCP server to the vibe coder and test each tool

connection.note: Server was picked up after a full restart of the Claude desktop app. Tools appear to the vibe coder namespaced as mcp__campus-customs-ops__<tool>.

database.unchanged_check: cmp data/campus_customs.db data/campus_customs_new.db -> identical; the three read-only tools wrote nothing

tests.prompt: Ticket 101 wants one Classic Bulldog Tee in size S. Do we have it in stock?

db_verification.sql: SELECT sku, size, qty, location FROM inventory WHERE sku='CC-TEE-WHITE' ORDER BY size;

tests.answer: No. Size S is at 0 units in Aisle B, so ticket 101 cannot be filled from stock — shortfall of 1.
tests.why_this_test_proves_the_tool_works: The SKU holds 10 units across L/M/XL, so a tool that ignored size would have reported the order as fillable. Returning qty_on_hand 0 for size S is the discriminating result.

tests.prompt: Ticket 102 is a rent notice on lease 1. How much is due, when, and can we cover it?

db_verification.sql: SELECT l.monthly_rent, l.next_due, d.date_today AS shop_today, CAST(julianday(l.next_due)-julianday(d.date_today) AS INT) AS days_until_due, c.balance, c.balance-l.monthly_rent AS after_rent FROM leases l, desk d, cash_accounts c WHERE l.id=1;

tests.answer: $2,400 to Elm City Properties for the Chapel Street shop, due 2026-09-02 — 2 days out, not yet late. Checking holds $3,400, so it is covered, leaving $1,000.
tests.why_this_test_proves_the_tool_works: The only tool reading three tables (leases + desk + cash_accounts), and the only one exercising the shop-clock rule. The real date at run time was 2026-10-12; had the tool used the system clock it would have reported rent ~40 days overdue instead of 2 days out. days_until_due 2 confirms it read desk.date_today.

tests.prompt: Ticket 103 wants 20 navy hoodies in M at 20% off list. What's the margin and is it above cost?

db_verification.sql: SELECT unit_cost, list_price, ROUND(20*58.0,2) AS rev_list, ROUND(20*unit_cost,2) AS cogs, ROUND(20*(58.0-unit_cost),2) AS gp_list, ROUND(100.0*(list_price-unit_cost)/list_price,1) AS margin_list, ROUND(20*46.40,2) AS rev_prop, ROUND(20*(46.40-unit_cost),2) AS gp_prop, ROUND(100.0*(46.40-unit_cost)/46.40,1) AS margin_prop FROM pricing WHERE sku='CC-HOOD-NAVY';

tests.answer: At $46.40/unit (20% off the $58 list) the margin is 52.6% — $928 revenue on $440 cost, $488 gross profit. Comfortably above the $22 break-even, giving up $232 versus list.
tests.why_this_test_proves_the_tool_works: Exercises the surface the other two do not: values computed over the ticket quantity rather than read from a row, plus the optional proposed_unit_price parameter. All nine derived figures reconcile to arithmetic over pricing.unit_cost and pricing.list_price.

result.summary: All three MCP tools were called by the vibe coder over stdio and every returned value reconciles to data/campus_customs_new.db by independent SQL. No value was invented and the database was not modified.
